-1.description: Does not fit any known pattern — older disks with high read error rates, many reallocated and pending sectors; majority are already failing.

0.description: Younger disks with below-average SMART errors and low age; some reallocated sectors present but overall behavior is stable.

1.description: Borderline group — nearly half of disks in this cluster failed; mixed health signals with no single dominant SMART pattern.

2.description: Newer disks but with very high pending and uncorrectable sector counts; command timeouts elevated — possible surface damage developing.

3.description: Critically dangerous — newer disks with an extreme number of pending sectors (avg 8384) but few reallocated sectors; nearly all (99.4%) are failing.

4.description: Low-moderate risk group; about 1 in 9 disks failing, no dominant distinguishing SMART pattern identified from available data.

5.description: Older disks with low error rates and low load cycle counts; aging naturally but SMART values are mostly within normal range.

6.description: Older disks with high reallocated sector counts but few pending sectors; degraded surface condition that has so far stabilised.

7.description: Youngest and cleanest disks — zero reallocated sectors, low error rates across all attributes; healthiest group in the dataset.

8.description: Younger disks with elevated reallocated sector count but low pending and read error rates; surface wear present but currently stable.

9.description: High failure rate group — over 83% of disks failing; likely represents a combination of advanced age and heavy SMART error accumulation.

10.description: Largest failure cluster — 95.5% failure rate across 1372 disks; dominant pattern of failed disks in the training data.

11.description: Moderate risk — about 1 in 5 disks failing; intermediate health state, worth monitoring closely.

12.description: Majority failing — 75% failure rate in a small but consistent cluster; likely a specific failure mode unique to a subset of disk models.

13.description: 86% of disks failing; small cluster representing a distinct high-risk SMART signature not seen in the evaluation CSV.

14.description: 86.8% failure rate — large high-risk cluster; disks placed here are very likely to fail based on their bottleneck feature pattern.

15.description: Near-certain failure — 97.9% of disks failed; second most dangerous named cluster, disks here are essentially at end of life.

16.description: 92.5% failure rate; compact cluster of disks with a specific failing SMART signature detected in the bottleneck space.

17.description: 93.7% failure rate — disks in this cluster share a high-risk bottleneck pattern consistent with late-stage disk degradation.
